authority: North York Moors National Park Authority
researched_by: the Authority's own car park pages, tariff table, car park terms and conditions and Share With Care guidance, plus Yorkshire Post reporting of the June 2026 moorland signage row
policy_summary:
No provision, and a prohibition built out of contract rather than law. The Authority runs eleven pay-and-display car parks - Cawthorn Roman Camps, Chop Gate, Danby Lodge, Goathland, Grosmont, Hole of Horcum (Saltergate), Hutton le Hole, Low Mill in Farndale, Newton under Roseberry, Sutton Bank and Thornton le Dale - and none of them has a designated motorhome space or an overnight scheme of any kind.

The distinctive thing here, and the reason this authority is not simply another closure regime, is that the Authority DOES sell an overnight ticket. The tariff table carries a 'Long stay parking' line reading 'Overnight parking of unoccupied vehicle - up to 24 hours GBP 7.20, up to 48 hours GBP 9.25', and the conditions of use say 'No Person shall park their vehicle overnight unless the car park tariff permits overnight parking. An overnight parking ticket is required to be purchased and displayed.' Overnight PARKING is therefore permitted and priced. Overnight OCCUPATION is not. The whole restriction rests on one word - unoccupied - and on the separate motorhome page, which is blunt: 'Unfortunately we do not have any designated spaces for these types of vehicles... Please remember that overnight parking is not allowed.' A walker leaving an empty car at Chop Gate for two nights on the Cleveland Way is a customer. The same person sleeping in a van beside it is in breach.

Compare Peak District, which closes every car park to every vehicle by byelaw between midnight and 6am, and Eryri, which shortens opening hours. North York Moors does neither. Its car parks have no published closing time, the pay-and-display terms 'apply 24 hrs per day and 7 days a week', and the only levers are the conditions of use - no tent, booth, stand or other structure without written consent, no fires or barbecues, no overnight parking without the right ticket - backed by a Parking Compliance Notice rather than a PCN under a traffic order or a prosecution under a byelaw. Newton under Roseberry is enforced by a private company, Total Parking Solutions, with its own charge and appeals portals. Motorhomes are explicitly on the list of vehicle types permitted to park by day; the objection is to the night, not the vehicle.

Outside the car parks the story of the last year is signage on private moorland. During late 2024 and 2025 the Authority put up 'no overnight parking' signs at Rosedale Bank Top, Blakey Bank Top and Hutton Common at the request of the Spaunton Estate, and at Danby Beacon on Dawnay Estates land, with the landowner adding permanent signs along the moor road between Egton Bridge and Rosedale Abbey. A photographer's post about them drew 1,200 comments in June 2026. The Authority's line is that there is no blanket ban - only specific spots where landowners asked - and its recreation director framed it as a landscape-impact problem: 'when there's 25 caravans placed in a very prominent spot it has a significant detrimental effect on what are the special qualities of the national park'. The estate's framing is wildfire, littering, anti-social behaviour and fouling, with the 40-day Langdale Moor fire as the example. Enforcement is trespass, pursued by the landowner if at all: 'legal action is always the last resort'.

Beyond that, wild camping is treated as unlawful without the landowner's permission - 'almost all land in the National Park is privately owned' - and campfires and barbecues are asked to be left at home entirely.
notes:
This is the weakest legal architecture of any national park in the dataset so far, and that is the finding. No car park byelaws were found - nothing like the Peak District's section 90 byelaws with a schedule of car parks and a level 2 fine, and no off-street parking order. What exists is a set of contractual conditions of use and a compliance notice. A byelaw breach is criminal; a compliance notice is a civil debt claim by a landowner. Forum users say exactly what you would expect of a regime with that much slack: a sign appeared at a popular spot, 'was duly ignored and no problem', and 'they cannot patrol it all'.

The direction of travel is tightening, but the tightening is being done by private estates with the Authority holding the screwdriver. Rosedale, Blakey, Hutton Common and Danby Beacon are all somebody else's land. The Authority erected the signs, took the public criticism, and simultaneously insisted it has imposed no blanket ban - which is legally accurate and does nothing for a driver deciding whether the sign in front of them means anything. Any map of restriction in this park is largely a map of private landowners' patience, not of instruments.

The framing difference from the neighbouring council is worth recording. North Yorkshire Council restricts motor caravans on the coast for resident amenity and does it with a permanent TRO and PCNs. The National Park Authority restricts on the moors for wildfire and landscape and does it with signs and a plea. Same county, same summer, two completely different theories of the problem.

OWNERSHIP TRAP, and it is a bad one here. Sandsend, Whitby and the coast north to Staithes are INSIDE the National Park boundary but the overnight motor caravan restrictions there are NORTH YORKSHIRE COUNCIL's - the permanent 11pm-7am motor caravan order on the A174 Sandsend-Raithwaite length, the legacy Whitby car park bans at Endeavour Wharf, Battery Parade and Marina, and the unauthorised camping PSPO covering the open space around Whitby Abbey. None of those is a National Park Authority measure and none is recorded here; see data/sites/north-yorkshire.json. Conversely the Authority owns land the council has nothing to do with, including the Levisham Estate. A van user standing in Whitby is inside a national park and subject to a unitary council's traffic order.

The most useful single fact for a van user is the one that reads like generosity: the Authority will take GBP 7.20 to leave a vehicle in its car park overnight, and GBP 9.25 for two nights. Buy that ticket and sleep in the van and you have paid for the evidence against yourself.
open_questions: A page at /plan-your-visit/car-parks-and-toilets/motorhome-bookings is indexed by search engines with the title 'Motorhome bookings | NYMNP' but returns HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt and is not linked from anywhere in the car parks section. It could be a new or upcoming motorhome overnight booking scheme, or a dead legacy page. It is the single biggest gap in this file and should be checked in a browser.

Whether the Authority has car park byelaws at all. The terms and conditions refer to complying with car park byelaws but none was found published, and no off-street parking order was found either. If byelaws exist the enforcement picture changes from civil to criminal.

Which of the eleven car parks the 'overnight parking of unoccupied vehicle' tariff is actually available at. The rate is published estate-wide but the conditions say overnight parking is only allowed 'unless the car park tariff permits' it, implying some car parks do not offer it. No per-car-park list was found.
Whether any Authority car park is gated or has a closing time. None is published, and the terms state the pay and display conditions apply 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

Coordinates for the four signed moorland spots - Rosedale Bank Top, Blakey Bank Top, Hutton Common and Danby Beacon. Named in the Yorkshire Post but no corroborated location source was reachable, so they are recorded as one zone record with null geometry rather than guessed at.

Thornton le Dale: the Authority's own map link centres on 54.23248,-0.72744 but pins 'Thornton Le Dale Car Park' at 54.23578,-0.72019, roughly 400m apart. The pin is used here and flagged approximate.
Height barriers and length limits. The motorhome page says space is limited and gives per-car-park advice on where to put a large vehicle, but publishes no dimensions.
Whether the Rosedale/Blakey signage has been escalated since June 2026, and whether the Authority intends any instrument behind it.

sites.name: All North York Moors National Park Authority car parks - overnight parking permitted only for an UNOCCUPIED vehicle
sites.notes: The governing rule for all eleven Authority car parks, and it is a tariff rather than a ban. The 'Long stay parking' line in the tariff table reads 'Overnight parking of unoccupied vehicle - up to 24 hours GBP 7.20, up to 48 hours GBP 9.25'. The conditions of use say 'No Person shall park their vehicle overnight unless the car park tariff permits overnight parking. An overnight parking ticket is required to be purchased and displayed.' So leaving a vehicle overnight is lawful, priced and encouraged - for walkers on the Cleveland Way and the long moorland routes it is a genuine product. Being INSIDE the vehicle is what the word 'unoccupied' excludes. Backed by the same conditions that prohibit erecting 'a tent, booth, stand, building or other structure in the car park without the Authority's written consent' and any fire or barbecue. Enforced by Parking Compliance Notice - a contractual charge, not a PCN under a traffic order and not a byelaw prosecution. No published closing time at any car park; the pay and display terms 'apply 24 hrs per day and 7 days a week, for every day of the year including Bank Holidays'.

sites.name: All North York Moors National Park Authority car parks - no motorhome or horsebox overnight parking
sites.notes: The motorhome and horsebox page closes the door that the unoccupied-vehicle tariff appears to open: 'Space is limited at some of our car parks for large motorhomes and horseboxes. Unfortunately we do not have any designated spaces for these types of vehicles... Please remember that overnight parking is not allowed.' Read together with the tariff, the position is that an empty car may stay the night for GBP 7.20 but a motorhome may not stay at all. Daytime parking is expressly fine - motorhomes are named in the conditions of use among the vehicle types permitted to park, and the page gives per-car-park advice on where to put one (coach bays at Danby Lodge, Thornton le Dale and Grosmont; the left of the entrance or the top area at Hutton le Hole; as space allows elsewhere; and at Sutton Bank 'do not use the car park on the Thirsk side (west) of the National Park Centre due to limited access width'). The objection is to the night, not the vehicle.

sites.name: Sutton Bank National Park Centre Car Park
sites.search_hint: Sutton Bank National Park Centre car park, A170 above Thirsk
sites.notes: The Authority's flagship site on the A170 escarpment - Changing Places facility, cafe, EV charging, and one of the great views in England, which is precisely why vans want to stay. GBP 3.90 up to 2 hours, GBP 6.20 over 2 hours, coaches GBP 7.50. An unoccupied vehicle may stay overnight on the GBP 7.20 ticket; a motorhome may not, and nobody may sleep. Large vehicles must use the main or coach area - the Authority specifically says do not use the car park on the Thirsk (west) side of the Centre because the access is too narrow. Visitor centre hours are roughly 10am-5pm but the car park itself has no published closing time.
sites.geocode_precision: Google Maps place pin for Sutton Bank National Park Centre, taken from the Authority's own map link on its car park list

sites.name: Danby Lodge National Park Centre Car Park
sites.search_hint: Danby Lodge National Park Centre car park, Lodge Lane, Danby
sites.notes: The Esk Valley centre on Lodge Lane, and the best-equipped Authority car park in the north of the park - eight EV chargers, cafe, toilets, cycle repair stand. GBP 3.90 up to 2 hours, GBP 6.20 over 2 hours, coaches GBP 7.50. Motorhomes are asked to use the coach parking area at weekends and in school holidays, and the main car park otherwise. Overnight only for an unoccupied vehicle on the GBP 7.20 ticket; motorhome overnight parking is not allowed. Danby Beacon, four miles north, is one of the moorland spots where the Authority has put up 'no overnight parking' signs at the landowner's request.
sites.geocode_precision: Google Maps destination pin for Danby Car Park, Lodge Lane, from the Authority's own map link

sites.name: Goathland Car Park (Beck Hole Road)
sites.search_hint: Goathland car park, Beck Hole Road, Goathland
sites.notes: Goathland is Heartbeat and Hogsmeade, one of the busiest honeypots in the park, and its car park is on a single flat rate of GBP 4.65 rather than the usual two-tier tariff - coaches GBP 7.50. On-site toilets. Motorhomes as space allows only; the Authority publishes no designated space. Overnight only for an unoccupied vehicle with the GBP 7.20 ticket, and not at all for a motorhome. Note the North Yorkshire Moors Railway runs its own car parks in the village and at Levisham and Grosmont - a different owner with different rules.
sites.geocode_precision: Google Maps destination pin for Goathland Car Park, Beck Hole Road, from the Authority's own map link

sites.name: Hutton le Hole Car Park (Moor Lane)
sites.search_hint: Hutton le Hole car park, Moor Lane, Hutton-le-Hole
sites.notes: GBP 4.65 up to 3 hours, GBP 6.20 over 3 hours, coaches GBP 7.50 - a three-hour first band rather than the usual two. Toilets and six EV chargers. The Authority gives unusually specific motorhome guidance here: motorhomes to the left of the entrance, horseboxes in the top parking area. Overnight only for an unoccupied vehicle; not for a motorhome. Hutton Common, just up the road on the Spaunton Estate, is one of the spots now signed 'no overnight parking' at the landowner's request - so the car park and the common carry different regimes and different owners a mile apart.

sites.name: Hole of Horcum Car Park (Saltergate)
sites.search_hint: Hole of Horcum Saltergate car park, A169 Pickering to Whitby
sites.notes: The Saltergate viewpoint on the A169 between Pickering and Whitby - a large open moor-top car park on a main road with a view into the Hole of Horcum, which makes it one of the most obvious overnight temptations in the park. GBP 3.90 up to 2 hours, GBP 6.20 over, coaches GBP 7.50. Facilities are two accessible portaloos and a refreshment van on some days. Motorhomes as space allows. Overnight only for an unoccupied vehicle with the GBP 7.20 ticket; a motorhome may not stay at all.
sites.geocode_precision: Google Maps place pin for Saltergate Car Park, from the Authority's own map link

sites.name: Newton under Roseberry Car Park
sites.search_hint: Newton under Roseberry car park, A173 for Roseberry Topping
sites.notes: The Roseberry Topping car park on the A173 at the northern edge of the park, and the one to be careful at: enforcement here is contracted out to TOTAL PARKING SOLUTIONS, with its own charge portal and its own appeals route, and it is the only Authority car park where late payment online is NOT accepted. GBP 3.90 up to 2 hours, GBP 6.20 over, coaches GBP 7.50. Toilets, six EV chargers. Motorhomes as space allows. Same overnight rules as the rest of the estate but with a private operator watching them.

sites.name: Grosmont Car and Coach Park (Front Street)
sites.search_hint: Grosmont car and coach park, Front Street, Grosmont
sites.notes: In the village at the northern terminus of the North Yorkshire Moors Railway. GBP 3.90 up to 2 hours, GBP 6.20 over, coaches GBP 7.50. Motorhomes as space allows or in the coach bays. Overnight only for an unoccupied vehicle; not for a motorhome. The railway's own station parking is separate and not an Authority car park.

sites.name: Chop Gate Car Park
sites.search_hint: Chop Gate car park, B1257 Bilsdale
sites.notes: On the B1257 in Bilsdale, a walkers' base for the Cleveland Hills and Wainstones. GBP 3.90 up to 2 hours, GBP 6.20 over. On-site toilets. This is exactly the kind of car park the 'overnight parking of unoccupied vehicle' tariff is designed for - GBP 9.25 covers a two-night walk. Sleeping in a vehicle here is not covered by that ticket.
sites.geocode_precision: coordinate pair set directly in the Authority's own Google Maps link for this car park

sites.name: Cawthorn Roman Camps Car Park
sites.search_hint: Cawthorn Roman Camps car park, near Cropton and Pickering
sites.notes: A remote forest-edge car park for the Roman camps above Cropton, GBP 3.90 up to 2 hours and GBP 6.20 over. No toilets on site - the nearest accessible toilets are at Pickering and need a RADAR key. Quiet, unlit and out of the way, which is why it matters that the estate rule applies here as everywhere: an unoccupied vehicle may stay, an occupied one may not.
sites.geocode_precision: coordinate pair set directly in the Authority's own Google Maps link for this car park

sites.name: Low Mill Car Park, Farndale
sites.search_hint: Low Mill car park, Farndale daffodil walk
sites.notes: The Farndale daffodil walk car park, and the only Authority car park with no tariff at all - a donation box instead. Toilets on site. In peak daffodil season a private overflow, the Daffy Car Park, also operates. Because there is no tariff there is no overnight ticket to buy, which means the conditions of use bite in their strict form: 'No Person shall park their vehicle overnight unless the car park tariff permits overnight parking.' On the face of it that makes Low Mill the one Authority car park where overnight parking is prohibited outright rather than merely conditioned on being unoccupied.

sites.name: Thornton le Dale Car Park (Maltongate)
facilities: four 75kW DC rapid EV chargers (2 accessible)
sites.search_hint: Thornton le Dale car park, Maltongate, Thornton-le-Dale
sites.notes: The only Authority car park with rapid DC charging - four 75kW units - which makes it the one most likely to attract a large vehicle for a long dwell. Three tariff bands: GBP 3.10 up to 1 hour, GBP 3.90 for 1-2 hours, GBP 6.20 over 2 hours, coaches GBP 7.50. Motorhomes are directed to the coach parking area. Confidence dropped to medium on location only: the Authority's own map link centres about 400m from the place pin it selects.

sites.name: Signed moorland stopping places: Rosedale Bank Top, Blakey Bank Top, Hutton Common and Danby Beacon
sites.search_hint: no overnight parking signs Rosedale Bank Top Blakey Ridge Danby Beacon
sites.notes:
'No overnight parking' signs erected by the National Park Authority from late 2024 into 2025 at Rosedale Bank Top, Blakey Bank Top and Hutton Common - all Spaunton Estate land, and all at the estate's request - and at Danby Beacon on Dawnay Estates land. The landowner has also put permanent signs along the moorland road between Egton Bridge and Rosedale Abbey. These are the classic Blakey Ridge and Rosedale moor-top viewpoints, and the row over them broke publicly in June 2026 when a photographer's post drew 1,200 comments and accusations of an 'attack on freedom'.

No order, no byelaw and no penalty sits behind the signs. The land is private, so the remedy is trespass and it belongs to the landowner, not the Authority. The Authority's recreation director Joel Brookfield: 'when there's 25 caravans placed in a very prominent spot it has a significant detrimental effect on what are the special qualities of the national park', and 'legal action is always the last resort and something you reach for when all other options are failed'. George Winn-Darley for Spaunton Estates cited wildfire, litter, anti-social behaviour and fouling, with the 40-day Langdale Moor fire as the example: 'the irresponsible ones can cause a huge amount of problems'.

The Authority is explicit that there is NO blanket overnight parking ban in the National Park - only these specific signed locations. Recorded as one zone record with null geometry because no corroborated coordinate source for the four individual laybys was reachable.

sites.name: Wild camping and sleeping out anywhere in the North York Moors National Park
sites.notes:
The Authority's Share With Care guidance is unambiguous: 'almost all land in the National Park is privately owned' and 'wild camping is unlawful without permission from the landowner'. Visitors are told to 'always use registered campsites', that some farmers and landowners may allow camping if asked, and - a harder line than most national parks take - 'do not light barbecues or campfires in the National Park', with camping stoves asked to be left at home altogether and a picnic suggested instead. That stove wording is a wildfire response, not a litter one: the park lost 40 days to the Langdale Moor fire, has had further fires at Fylingdales, and has attracted GBP 3.2m of government wildfire recovery funding.

The Authority does own land of its own, notably the 3,000-acre Levisham Estate, an SSSI where it has publicly pursued illegal off-roading and trespass. Nothing published suggests any Authority-owned land is open to overnight vehicle stays. There is no aire, no campervan bay and no Authority-run campsite anywhere in this national park - unlike the Peak District, which at least runs North Lees.
